question.leadin: Give the following about the history of Mexico.
question.text: At its height, this center of the Aztec empire has been estimated to be one of the largest cities in the world. Mexico City was built on its ruins.
question.clue: Its inhabitants engaged in "flower wars" with its neighbors in order to provide captives for human sacrifice, and the Tlaxcala feuded with this city-state.

swap.text: This Aztec emperor exchanged gifts with Cortez at Cortez's first arrival before his eventual defeat.
swap.clue: Early in his campaign, Cortes captured this Aztec emperor and attempt to rule Mexico through him. The details of this man's captivity and eventual death remain unclear.

question.text: One major Postclassic Mayan city was this one in the northern Yucatan, which contains the Castillo and the Caracol, an observatory, as well as two large cenotes.
question.clue: This location was once part of a league with neighboring Uxmal .

swap.leadin: The Pecos Classification divides these people's history into early "basketmaker" eras and later periods which included Pope's Rebellion.
swap.text: Name these people of the Southwestern U.S. who are the ancestors of tribes like the Hopi and Zuni. These people were named by the Spanish for the adobe communities they built at sites like Mesa Verde.
swap.answerHtml: Ancestral Pueblo [or Puebloans; or Anasazi; or Chaco; accept the Pueblo Revolt; prompt on the San Juan Valley Culture]
swap.clue: This culture's "Bonito Phase" is named for the biggest of its "Great Houses" like Casa Rinconada.

question.text: Under the direction of Enrico Martinez, the Spanish conquerors of Tenochtitlan drained this body of water upon which the city was built.

swap.text: The earliest known Mesoamerican ballcourt is in San Lorenzo, a site from this culture. The ballgame was probably invented by this Formative Period culture, which also created many colossal stone heads.
swap.clue: Archaeologists call its most significant city San Lorenzo, and one of its pyramids called Complex C is found in La Venta.

question.text: This Mayan city in modern-day Guatemala had a long-standing feud with Calakmul (kah-laak-MOOL). This city's Plaza of the Seven Temples has an unusual triple ballcourt.
question.clue: This polity's rival was called the Snake Kingdom, and this polity's namesake hiatus began after its ruler Wak Chan K'awiil was defeated by this polity's rival and Caracol.

swap.leadin: Who here likes guns? Apparently, not the Aztecs.
swap.text: The Aztecs were conquered by a mix of guns, Tlaxcalan Indians, and the sheer willpower of this conquistador who in 1521 besieged Tenochtitlan and effectively destroyed the Aztec Empire.
swap.clue: This Spaniard conquered the Aztec Empire. He destroyed his own ships to encourage his men to press on.

question.leadin: Some "conquest slabs" at this site have been identified at its Building J.
question.text: Name this archaeological site in Oaxaca, Mexico, the socioeconomic center of the erstwhile Zapotec culture.
question.clue: Another monument depicts men with scrolls in place of their genitalia who likely represent mutilated war captives - that being the Temple of the Danzantes, or the "Building of the Dancers."

swap.text: The shrine at Chan Santa Cruz for the talking cross was built around one of these places. These water-filled caves and sinkholes have a name from Yucatec Maya.
swap.clue: Along with caves, these natural features were considered sacred by the Maya as entrances to Xibalba [shee-ball-BAH] and were often used for human sacrifices.

question.leadin: Arthur Anderson and Charles Dibble made the first full English translation of this 12-book work after it was rediscovered by the scholar Angelo Bandini.
question.text: Name this text preserved in the Laurentian library. It was composed by the missionary Bernardino de Sahagun in conjunction with his students in Tlatelolco.
question.clue: Preserved in the Laurentian library, this text provided historians with knowledge about the culture of the Aztec empire. La Malinche or Donna Marina interpreted this text for Hernan Cortes.

swap.leadin: According to the Spanish, the Mexica people killed Moctezuma II during this event.
swap.text: Name this 1520 event in which forces under Cuitlahuac ("kweet-LA-wock") were able to chase out Hernan Cortes's men. Many Spanish soldiers drowned during this event due to the weight of the gold they had plundered.
swap.answerHtml: La Noche Triste (“la no-CHAY tree-STAY”) [or the Sad Night; or the Night of Sorrows]
swap.clue: After Moctezuma's death, Cortes attempted to flee the Aztec capital in this event, but suffered heavy losses and a personal wound while doing so.

question.leadin: Answer the following about archaeoacoustics, a field concerned with the acoustics of archaeological sites and artifacts.
question.text: Researchers have noted that clapping hands near this civilization's Kukulkan pyramid produces a "chirping" sound reminiscent of the quetzal bird. Kukulkan is located in the ruins of this civilization's city of Chichen Itza.
question.answerHtml: Maya civilization [accept word forms like Mayan or more specific answers, like Late Classic Maya]
question.clue: The Izapan culture was a major predecessor to this civilization, which was not conquered by the Spanish until 1541 by Pedro de Alvarado.

swap.leadin: City centres of this civilisation included Caracol, initially a client state of Tikal.
swap.text: Name this Mesoamerican civilisation centred in modern-day Guatemala, Belize, and surrounding regions. This civilisation most notably used the Long Count calendar.
swap.clue: This civilisation's southern city of Chocola rose to prominence as a production centre of cacao beans.

question.leadin: Answer the following about some North American ruins.
question.text: This Mayan city is located in the western portion of Honduras. It was ruled by the awesomely named Xukpi Kingdom, as well as someone name 18 Rabbit.
question.clue: An extremely long text comprised of over 2,000 glyphs is found at this site's "Hieroglyphic Stairway."

swap.text: This elegant cavalry tactic was notably not employed by the New Model Army and Gustavus Adolphus's hakkapeliitta cavalry. It had cavalry form up in ranks to discharge pistols, reform at the rear to reload, and repeat.

question.leadin: Toward the end of their empire, Aztec rulers would travel to this city to be anointed by its priests.
question.text: Name this second-largest Aztec city, which was home to an enormous "Great Pyramid" and which was the site of a notorious 1519 massacre.
question.clue: This still-inhabited city, found in the metropolitan district of Puebla, contains a building which was said to have been built by the Quinametzin ("kee-nah-MET-zeen") giants.

swap.text: Jeronimo de Aguilar, shipwrecked on the coast of the Yucatan, made it possible for Spaniards to communicate with this woman, a slave among the people of Tabasco who then became a translator.
swap.clue: After their defeat at Potonchan, the Maya gifted 20 women including this Nahua slave to Hernan Cortes. This woman served as a translator during Cortes' conquest of the Aztecs..

question.leadin: Answer the following about "Dual-Processual Theory" of Mesoamerican archaeology.
question.text: The theory uses thiscihuacoatl's[kih-wuh-KWAH-tull] centering of Aztec ideology on the Flower Wars to exemplify both strategies. This general organized his uncle Itzcoatl [its-KWAH-tull] I's book-burnings to wipe out knowledge of prior history.
question.clue: This Mesoamerican political leader who served as the first cihuacoatl ("see-wa-CO-aht"), or "female serpent", an office which served as the chief deputy of the Aztec emperor.

swap.text: An account of the destruction of Tenochtitlan by Cortes was also made by this friar, whose massive work, General History of the Things of New Spain, is often referred to as the "Florentine Codex."
swap.clue: This Franciscan friar translated and annotated the Florentine Codex with help from students at the Colegio de Santa Cruz.
